title: Testing the Visual Field

patient.name: Mdm Hamidah bte Othman
patient.presenting_complaint: Referred for Humphrey Visual Field test — elevated IOP, glaucoma suspect

history.hpc: Mdm Hamidah was seen in OPD and found to have elevated IOP (right eye 26 mmHg, left eye 24 mmHg) on two separate occasions. She has no visual symptoms — no tunnel vision, no peripheral vision loss that she is aware of. She has been referred for a Humphrey Visual Field (HVF) test to assess whether any functional loss is present. She has never had an HVF done before and is unsure what it involves.
history.family_hx: Father diagnosed with glaucoma in his 60s
history.social_hx: Office worker. Right-handed. Wears reading glasses.

examination_findings.anterior_segment: Normal bilaterally. No disc pallor on fundus exam documented by doctor.
examination_findings.fundus: C:D ratio 0.6 bilaterally (noted by doctor) — borderline suspicious

hvf_right.reliability: Fixation losses 1/14 (7%), False positive 2%, False negative 1%
hvf_right.result: Within normal limits. No definite scotoma.

hvf_left.reliability: Fixation losses 0/14, False positive 1%, False negative 3%
hvf_left.result: Within normal limits. Borderline early superior depression — to correlate with disc.

diagnosis: HVF SITA Standard 24-2 performed on both eyes. Reliable tests. No confirmed glaucomatous field defect. Borderline findings in left eye to be correlated with disc appearance by doctor.

immediate: Confirm patient identity and which eyes are to be tested
Explain the HVF test procedure to patient in clear terms
Set up HVF machine: enter patient data, select programme (24-2 SITA Standard as ordered)
Position patient comfortably with chin on chinrest, forehead on forehead rest
Patch the eye not being tested
Ensure correct trial lens inserted if patient wears glasses (based on age and prescription)
Demonstrate the test: click button when light seen, do not move eye, stare at central fixation light
Run the test, monitor for fixation losses and reliability
Print report and hand to doctor
follow_up: Doctor to correlate HVF result with disc appearance and IOP trend
If glaucoma confirmed, start IOP-lowering treatment
Repeat HVF in 6 months for monitoring
patient_education: Explain this is a map of what she can see — no right or wrong answers
Tell her to respond honestly, even if not sure
Advise test takes 6-10 minutes per eye
Tell her to inform OT if she needs to stop or rest

key_points: Confirms patient identity and eyes to be tested
Asks if patient has done HVF before (first-timers need more explanation and may have a learning effect)
Checks if patient wears glasses — correct trial lens needed for accurate HVF
Explains the procedure clearly before starting the test
Selects correct HVF programme as ordered (SITA Standard 24-2)
Enters patient data accurately into machine
Positions patient correctly on chinrest with appropriate correction in the trial frame
Patches untested eye and monitors patient for fixation loss during test
Prints report and checks reliability indices (fixation losses, false positives/negatives)
Identifies whether test is reliable (fixation losses <20%, false positives <15%)
Recognises that an unreliable test may need to be repeated
Does not interpret clinical significance independently — refers to doctor
Identifies purpose: to map peripheral vision for glaucoma assessment
Documents test results and prints report accurately
Educates patient in a way that reduces anxiety and improves cooperation during test
Checks reliability before dismissing patient — repeat if test unreliable
